description: This article by a forensic engineering firm describes four investigations of broadcast equipment failures in insurance claims. The first found that an elevated VSWR blamed on lightning came from arcing in poorly maintained sections of an FM transmission line; the second traced weather-dependent range to an antenna detuned after protective radomes were removed and fixed by electronic retuning; the third followed a transmitter off air for about three days after a power surge, where earlier damaged surge protection failed and the station returned within nine days; the fourth found that after a tornado most site equipment was hermetically sealed and safe from water. Producer: Envista Forensics, published 11 October 2024, with background on installations (tower, lighting, de-icing, guy wires, generator) and causes such as lightning, heat, ice, ageing and rodents. Coverage: US broadcast sites, unnamed. Access: free web page. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: cases are anonymised and undated, give no numbers of stations or costs, and come from a commercial forensic firm. Simulation uses: the failure modes and repair times give scenario inputs for broadcast site reliability and resilience studies. Related records: none linked.
